findings.title: Error-focused query check uses substring matching and can transform transaction queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` only checks whether `event.type:error` appears anywhere in the lowercased `query` URL parameter. This matches queries such as `!event.type:error` (selects non-error events) or `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` (mixed errors and transactions). When it returns true, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` replaces `count()` with `upsampled_count()`, which emits `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. `sample_weight` is only valid for error events, so these queries can fail in Snuba or return incorrect counts. Parse the actual query filter structure instead of using a substring.

findings.title: Upsampling decision is based on the URL query, not the actual query being executed
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` has a `query` argument but calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` without passing it; the helper instead reads `request.GET['query']`. The dashboard split path calls `_get_event_stats` with derived queries such as `({query}) AND !event.type:transaction` and `({query}) AND event.type:transaction`. Therefore the upsampling transformation can be applied to a transaction-only derived query or skipped for an errors-only derived query based on the original URL query, causing `sum(sample_weight)` to run against an inappropriate event set. The decision should use the same query string passed to the dataset query builder.

findings.title: Top events are ordered by raw count, not upsampled count
findings.body: In the `top_events > 0` branch, only `timeseries_columns`/`y_axes` are transformed to `upsampled_count()`; `selected_columns` and `orderby` are still obtained from the original request, typically `-count()`. The top groups are therefore selected and ranked by raw event counts while their timeseries values are upsampled. If the allowlisted projects or events have different `sample_rate` values, the top-N groups can be the wrong groups. The orderby and count fields used for top-event selection should be transformed consistently.

findings.title: Allowlist cache invalidation is never called
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but no caller is added in this PR. Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. If a project is removed from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, existing cache entries can remain `True` for up to 60 seconds, causing queries for no-longer-allowlisted projects to be transformed to `sum(sample_weight)` even though `sample_weight` may not be valid for them. Wire this invalidation into the allowlist update path or remove the cache.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public SnQL function and bypasses allowlist/dataset checks
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is added to `function_converter` without `private=True`. A client can therefore request `yAxis=upsampled_count()` directly; the endpoint will pass it to Snuba without going through `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` or the error-only query check. On a transaction query or a project that is not allowlisted, this still builds `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, which can fail or produce invalid data. Mark it private/internal so only the server-side transformation can emit it.

findings.title: Accidental submodule/gitlink file committed
findings.body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`, i.e. a gitlink/submodule entry. This appears unrelated to the feature and can break clones or CI because there is no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. Remove this accidental repository link before merging.
